stances.claim: The 'most extreme' competing view -- from retired RTC Judge Frank Lobrigo -- is that the BIR can unilaterally 'abate taxes that are excessive or unjust' under Section 204 NIRC without need of reopening Marcos II v. CA (June 5, 2007), and that the President has no power to appoint an independent body to review BIR findings; after abatement, the Marcos estate could file an estate tax return anew and avail of the current estate tax amnesty.

'With due respect,' CJ maintains his three-item position: (1) the BIR should advise the public of the status of estate-tax collection; (2) the President can and should appoint an independent body to determine the truth and validity of imposed taxes; (3) the SC, upon initiative of Marcos heirs, can review the findings of that independent body.
stances.confidence: asserted with 'with due respect' deference marker

stances.claim: Item 1 is reinforced by Estrella V. Martinez's January 17, 2007 letter to then Finance Secretary Margarito Teves disclosing that 'in partial settlement of the tax liabilities of Ferdinand Marcos and Imelda Romualdez Marcos,' she forfeited 10 parcels of land originally titled in Imelda's name -- meaning the original P23 billion (and 'ballooned' P203 billion) may no longer be accurate, other Marcos properties may have been levied and sold, and 'All the BIR Commissioners from 1999 to 2022 have remained silent.'

Item 2 -- presidential independent body -- is grounded in the President's 'constitutional power of control over the entire executive branch,' analogous to the way PFM created the Agrava Board to investigate the Ninoy Aquino murder. Former SGV chair Cirilo Noel corroborated via text: PH cannot rely 'simply on the BIR's table assessment. This requires a factual determination by an independent body as you proposed.'
stances.rhetorical_move: constitutional-authority anchor + Agrava analogy + corroborator text

stances.claim: Item 3 -- SC review -- is necessary because the Marcos II v. CA decision became final and executory, affirming the P23 billion tax liability. Abatement or modification 'cannot be done -- as a matter of law or at least of judicial courtesy -- without the SC's imprimatur.' The SC can create its own fact-finding body (per Galman v. Sandiganbayan, Sept. 12, 1986, with retired SC Justice Conrado Vazquez as chair, retired CA Justice Milagros German, and lawyer Eduardo Caguioa) or appoint a 'Special Master' (per retired SC Justice Adolfo S. Azcuna's text suggestion) to help resolve factual needs.

Together, these three items are needed to determine 'whether there is a miscarriage of justice in the imposition and collection of the Marcos estate taxes' -- bypassing neither the BIR (item 1) nor the executive (item 2) nor the judiciary (item 3).

Retired CJ Lucas P. Bersamin's acceptance of the executive-secretary post is 'patriotic and courageous': patriotic for serving under a head a 'rank lower in the officialdom than his prior post as the chief of a constitutionally coequal branch,' to help the President minimize poverty/inflation/joblessness/ill-health, protect from criminality and foreign incursions, promote general welfare, and uphold constitutional rights; courageous for 'entering the political arena without the protective shields granted by the Constitution to the judiciary,' relying only on continuing presidential trust 'to fend off the intrigues of political warlords and the jealousy of charlatans.'

notable_anecdotes: Lobrigo's 'gallant' non-partisan disclosure -- 'did not vote for (PBBM), (he would) accept if the estate tax issue is settled in accordance with the NIRC, whether the BIR enforces it or abates it' -- capturing the retired judge's deliberate principled posture toward an unfavored president.

Estrella V. Martinez's Jan 17, 2007 letter to Finance Sec. Teves disclosing partial settlement via forfeiture of 10 parcels originally titled to Imelda -- making concrete that the 'P23 billion' headline figure has not been static and that the public has not been told about parallel settlements.

Reader Jose Oliveros's pointed observation -- 'All the BIR Commissioners from 1999 to 2022 have remained silent' -- converting a reader's email into a 23-year-silence indictment of BIR public communication.

The Agrava Board analogy -- PFM created an independent fact-finding body to investigate Ninoy Aquino's murder during his own administration -- using a precedent from the Marcos Sr. era to legitimate independent-body creation by the Marcos Jr. administration.

Cirilo Noel (former SGV chair) text corroboration -- 'simply on the BIR's table assessment' is insufficient; 'factual determination by an independent body as you proposed' -- a top-tier-accounting-firm-chair endorsement of CJ's position by text message.

Galman v. Sandiganbayan SC fact-finding commission preserved with full membership -- retired SC Justice Conrado Vazquez (chair), retired CA Justice Milagros German, lawyer Eduardo Caguioa -- making the precedent operationally specific and replicable.
Retired SC Justice Adolfo S. Azcuna's Special Master text suggestion -- adding an alternative mechanism (Special Master, drawn from US federal-court practice) to the SC's fact-finding toolkit.
The 'P23 billion (that had allegedly ballooned to P203 billion)' framing -- parenthetical preservation of the disputed ballooning figure that has dominated political discourse.

The Bersamin postscript -- 'patriotic because he would be serving under the head of the executive branch, a rank lower in the officialdom than his prior post as the chief of a constitutionally coequal branch' -- making explicit the hierarchical asymmetry CJ Bersamin accepted in moving from CJ to executive secretary.
The 'intrigues of political warlords and the jealousy of charlatans' phrase -- CJ's signature alliterative concern about the political arena, applied to the new executive-secretary post.
'May the Lord bless him in his new journey of service to our nation' -- religious-blessing closer giving the Bersamin tribute spiritual weight.

one_paragraph_summary: Following his prior Monday column on PBBM's desire to reopen the P23 billion (allegedly ballooned to P203 billion) Marcos estate tax imposed by the BIR, Panganiban surveys the reactions. The 'most extreme' is from retired RTC Judge Frank Lobrigo, who asserted that the BIR can -- on its own authority under Section 204 NIRC -- 'abate taxes that are excessive or unjust' without needing to reopen Marcos II v. CA (June 5, 2007), which 'merely affirmed' the CA's verdict upholding the BIR's 'summary remedy (levy and sale of the taxpayer's assets)' for assessments that 'had already attained finality.' Lobrigo argued the President has no power to appoint an independent body to review the BIR's findings; 'gallantly,' he disclosed he 'did not vote for (PBBM)' but would accept settlement per the NIRC 'whether the BIR enforces it or abates it' -- after which 'the Marcos estate can file an estate tax return anew and avail itself of the current estate tax amnesty.' 'With due respect,' CJ maintains his three-item position: (1) the BIR should publicly advise on the status of estate-tax collection; (2) the President can and should appoint an independent body to determine the truth and validity of imposed taxes; (3) the SC, on the Marcos heirs' initiative, can review that body's findings. On item 1, he relays Estrella V. Martinez's January 17, 2007 letter to then Finance Secretary Margarito Teves disclosing that 'in partial settlement of the tax liabilities of Ferdinand Marcos and Imelda Romualdez Marcos,' she had forfeited 10 parcels of land originally titled to Imelda -- meaning the original P23 billion (and the 'balloon' figure) may no longer be accurate, other Marcos properties may have been levied and sold, and as reader Jose Oliveros observed, 'All the BIR Commissioners from 1999 to 2022 have remained silent.' On item 2, the President's authority arises from his 'constitutional power of control over the entire executive branch' to create an independent body, analogous to PFM's own creation of the Agrava Board to investigate the Ninoy Aquino murder; former SGV chair Cirilo Noel texted that PH cannot rely 'simply on the BIR's table assessment. This requires a factual determination by an independent body as you proposed.' On item 3, the SC decision became final and executory and affirmed the P23 billion tax liability; abatement or modification 'cannot be done -- as a matter of law or at least of judicial courtesy -- without the SC's imprimatur.' The SC can create its own fact-finding body following the model of Galman v. Sandiganbayan (September 12, 1986), where the commission was composed of retired SC Justice Conrado Vazquez (chair), retired CA Justice Milagros German, and lawyer Eduardo Caguioa; alternatively, per retired SC Justice Adolfo S. Azcuna's text, a 'Special Master' can be appointed. Together these three items determine 'whether there is a miscarriage of justice in the imposition and collection of the Marcos estate taxes.' In a postscript, CJ congratulates retired CJ Lucas P. Bersamin for his 'patriotic and courageous' acceptance of the executive-secretary post -- patriotic for serving under the President at 'a rank lower in the officialdom than his prior post as the chief of a constitutionally coequal branch,' helping minimize poverty/inflation/joblessness/ill-health and uphold constitutional rights; courageous for 'entering the political arena without the protective shields granted by the Constitution to the judiciary,' relying only on continuing presidential trust 'to fend off the intrigues of political warlords and the jealousy of charlatans.' 'May the Lord bless him in his new journey of service to our nation.'
